I did some testing and here are my findings:

For one, if a message is sent to a subverse and a mod of that subverse clicks on their "my messages" icon, they will be sent automatically to the summary page instead of the inbox, and thus will be able to see they have modmail. I did not confirm that this happens multiple times, but it does happen at least once. If you are receiving modmail but not getting sent automatically to the summary page, it probably means that some other mod was sent to the page and did not read the modmail.

Secondly, there is a BUG with respect to SMail and user mail, and I think we actually identified this way back when when testing on the preview, though I may be misremembering. At any rate, the BUG is as follows:

If a user sends mail directly to a subverse (e.g. /u/user sends a message to /v/subverse), /v/subverse will receive the message from /u/user in the SMail successfully.

If a mod (e.g. /u/mod) replies to the message that /u/user sent to /v/subverse, the BUG kicks in. Instead of the reply being of the form /v/subverse (/u/mod) > /u/user, the reply will be of the form /v/mod (/u/mod) > /u/user. Notice the difference? The reply is sent from /v/mod (which may or may not even exist) by the user /u/mod to the original message sender /u/user.

/u/user will still receive the reply (I think; this is at least the case if /v/mod exists; it may not be the case if /v/mod does not exist). However, because the reply was sent by /v/mod (/u/mod) instead of by /v/subverse (/u/mod) as it should have been, if a moderator of /v/subverse looks in the "Sent" tab of /v/subverse's SMail, they will not see the message as being sent, because it was not sent from /v/subverse, but from /v/mod.

I think that should account for the issues you were experiencing. This is repeatable (at least so long as /v/mod exists). I don't know if the messages are still sent if /v/mod exists, but the same BUG is taking effect, since your personal replies are not being sent.

It's one reason I recommend all users (especially if they moderate subverses) create a subverse in their own name.
